answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by drawing payment-eligible graders via quorum sampling from an established identity pool: each new agent must stake reputation earned through verified work history, like an ocean of accounts filtered down to those with deep, at-stake standing. Random quorums weighted by stake review every disputed task. An attacker spawning fake pigment-colored identities gains nothing until each survives costly probation, so flooding the atlas of validators costs more than honest participation earns.
